hook: SCP-3838 is about eight nomadic Turkmen tribes who share the same small patch of land near the Caspian Sea, each living in a different stretch of history. They treat centuries like pastureland, to be grazed, traded over and raided. Take your time with the tribe table; most of the worldbuilding lives there, and small details in it pay off later.
whyItMatters: It sets a Foundation file on the Central Asian steppe, complete with khans, begs, gers and a precursor organisation that began inside the Safavid government. The idea of time as territory is carried through consistently, from raids and a shared marketplace era to tribes pushed back by a stronger neighbour. It also treats the Foundation's relationship with the tribes as diplomacy rather than pure containment, with protection traded for technology from the future.
thingsToNotice:
The table seeds a mystery in passing: the fourth tribe guards a funeral urn holding a 'fallen foe', the second tribe's oral tradition mentions an ancient urn, the seventh tribe's elders say they lost theirs, and an antique urn with shifting markings turns up for sale in the marketplace. Behind all of it sit the great battle just before the Holy Years and the eighth tribe in the far future, whom no one at the Foundation has ever met.

The envoy interview reframes the villains. The skin-wearing, expansionist fourth tribe says it is holding something prisoner, split across another reality, another concept of existence and a pocket of time, and begs the Foundation, the Jailors, to broker peace because the other tribes have forgotten. Callaghan's song, said to come from the eighth tribe, then speaks in the prisoner's own voice about seven seals and seven tribes, six reclaimed, and a Crimson Khan who will ride before the end, which ties the article to its scarlet-king tag.
